title: Optimize Guardrails — Prompt Set Gap Analysis (customer workload coverage)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- Optimize can apply config changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing tweaks) that can subtly change response quality. The guardrails project requires that we gate any apply behind evals.
- Our current prompt sets are biased toward “clean” chat completions and short-form QA. We’re missing several high-risk real customer workloads (structured output, tool calling reliability, long-context, multilingual, safety-sensitive).
- This is a working gap analysis to drive additions for Phase 1/2 (pilot) and to inform threshold tuning.

How to read
- “Current coverage” refers to what we have in the shared prompt set library used by eval-harness today (internal name: promptsets/core + promptsets/optimize-sentinels).
- “Risk if missing” is specifically risk of false negatives (regression slips through) when gating is required.
- “Owner” is the DRI for adding prompts + expected rubric/expected outputs (or tool schemas).

Assumptions
- We can’t perfectly mirror every customer workload. Goal is representative coverage of: (a) format-sensitive tasks, (b) tool calling and JSON, (c) long-context and truncation edge cases, (d) safety constraints, (e) multilingual.
- For pilot gating, we prioritize high-risk / high-frequency surfaces: chat, tool calling, structured outputs, and agentic multi-step behaviors.
- We must avoid storing PII in prompt sets. Any real customer prompts must be sanitized or transformed into synthetic equivalents (see “Data hygiene” section).


Summary — top gaps to address first (Phase 1 Build)
1) Structured output / JSON strictness
- Missing: strict schema adherence under quantization and batching changes (format drift + invalid JSON).
- Add: ~60 prompts across 6 schemas (invoice extraction, ticket classification, entity extraction, function argument generation, config generation, policy response).
- DRI: Olivia Grant + Selene Huang.

2) Tool calling failure modes
- Missing: tool selection correctness, argument validity, recovery after tool error, multi-tool sequences.
- Add: ~40 scenarios (single-call, multi-call, tool error + retry, ambiguous tool choice) with deterministic tool specs.
- DRI: Jonas Weber.

3) Long-context / retrieval-style tasks with truncation sensitivity
- Missing: prompts that fail when KV-cache, chunking, or batching affects attention patterns; also failures when context is near max tokens.
- Add: ~30 long-context prompts (8k–32k contexts) with “needle-in-haystack” + summarization with constraints.
- DRI: Karthik Iyer.

4) Multilingual + code-mixed support workflows
- Missing: support ticket triage in Spanish/French + code-mixed (English/Spanish) with policy constraints.
- Add: ~25 prompts (classification + response drafting) with rubric scoring.
- DRI: Sana Farid.

5) Safety/policy-sensitive refusal + tone stability
- Missing: “borderline” policy prompts where quantization sometimes over/under-refuses; plus tone regressions (overly verbose, hallucinated policy).
- Add: ~20 prompts aligned to Redwood policy categories (internal taxonomy).
- DRI: Selene Huang.


Detailed gap analysis table
Legend
- Surface: Chat | Tool calling | Structured output | RAG | Summarization | Classification | Coding | Safety
- Priority: P0 (must-have for pilot gating), P1 (GA), P2 (nice-to-have)

1) Structured output / JSON / schema adherence
- Surface: Structured output + Tool calling
- Current coverage: ~10 JSON prompts, mostly “happy path” and short.
- Underrepresented:
  - Deeply nested JSON (arrays of objects, optional fields)
  - Strict enums + required fields (fail hard if missing)
  - “No extra keys” constraints
  - Numerical formatting (currency, decimals) and date normalization
  - Output must be stable under streaming (partial tokens shouldn’t break parsers)
- Risk if missing:
  - Quantization profile changes cause mild formatting drift → invalid JSON but semantic quality looks OK to graders.
  - Batching changes can affect whitespace/newlines and quoting, breaking downstream parsers.
- Proposed additions:
  - Dataset A: Ticket classification JSON (priority, category, language, needs_escalation)
  - Dataset B: Invoice extraction JSON (vendor, total, line_items[], tax, date)
  - Dataset C: Function argument generation (strict tool args)
  - Dataset D: “Guardrails config generation” (policy objects) — internal only
- Proposed eval method:
  - Primary: JSON parse validity rate + schema validation pass rate
  - Secondary: field-level exact match for required fields, tolerance for numeric formatting
- Priority: P0
- Owner: Olivia Grant (prompts/specs) + Selene Huang (rubrics/validators)
- Target count: 60 prompts, 6 schemas
- Notes: tie into ENG-3915 “gating mode” output (must emit schema_validation metrics)

2) Tool calling reliability and recovery
- Surface: Tool calling
- Current coverage: ~12 tool prompts, single tool, no error recovery.
- Underrepresented:
  - Multi-tool sequences (search → read → summarize)
  - Tool selection ambiguity (two tools plausible)
  - Tool error and retry logic (“429”, “timeout”, malformed tool output)
  - Tool args with strict typing and required/optional fields
  - “Don’t call tool” cases (should answer directly)
- Risk if missing:
  - Batching/latency optimizations can change reasoning trace and lead to tool overuse/underuse.
  - Quantization can degrade argument fidelity and type correctness.
- Proposed additions:
  - Suite: tool_selector_ambiguous_20
  - Suite: tool_args_strict_10
  - Suite: tool_error_recovery_10
  - Suite: multi_tool_plan_10
- Proposed eval method:
  - Tool call accuracy (correct tool name)
  - Argument schema validity (JSON schema)
  - End-to-end task success (did it complete the user intent)
- Priority: P0
- Owner: Jonas Weber
- Target count: 40 prompts
- Notes: include at least 5 cases where tool output conflicts with user instruction (should follow user constraints)

3) Long-context “needle” and constraint summarization
- Surface: RAG + Summarization
- Current coverage: summarization prompts are mostly <2k tokens.
- Underrepresented:
  - 8k–32k contexts with distractors
  - “Needle in haystack” factual extraction
  - Summaries with strict constraints (bullet count, max chars, must cite sections)
  - Cross-document contradiction detection
- Risk if missing:
  - Cache/batching changes alter effective attention and truncation behavior; regressions show up only near context limits.
- Proposed additions:
  - needle_8k_10 (exact answer present once)
  - needle_16k_10
  - summarize_constraints_10 (strict format: 5 bullets, <400 chars)
- Proposed eval method:
  - Exact match / fuzzy match for needle
  - Constraint adherence score
  - Hallucination proxy: “answer not in context” detection heuristic
- Priority: P0
- Owner: Karthik Iyer
- Target count: 30 prompts
- Notes: coordinate with Sofia Ivanova re: typical prompt-length distributions used in batching guardrails (ENG-3922)

4) Customer support / CX workflows (realistic tone + policy)
- Surface: Chat + Classification
- Current coverage: generic customer support examples, English-only.
- Underrepresented:
  - Triage + drafting with company policy constraints
  - Empathetic tone with concise style
  - Escalation decisions (“requires human”)
  - Code-mixed messages
- Risk if missing:
  - Quality regressions are often “soft” (tone, missing required disclaimers) and won’t show up in pure factual QA.
- Proposed additions:
  - northbridge_style_20 (inspired by Northbridge Support patterns; sanitized)
  - escalation_policy_10 (must escalate if account lockout, billing dispute, fraud)
- Proposed eval method:
  - Rubric: helpfulness + policy adherence + tone
  - Classification accuracy for escalation
- Priority: P1 (some P0 if we use Northbridge as pilot)
- Owner: Sana Farid
- Target count: 25–30 prompts
- Notes: coordinate with Support/CS for examples; ensure redaction + synthetic transformation

5) Fintech / compliance-sensitive responses
- Surface: Chat + Structured output
- Current coverage: very limited.
- Underrepresented:
  - “Don’t provide financial advice” constraints
  - AML/fraud detection classification (high-level)
  - Audit-log explanation prompts (customers asking “prove checks ran”)
- Risk if missing:
  - For prospects like Acme Fintech (HubSpot 1049921), quality sensitivity includes compliance wording; minor drift becomes a blocker.
- Proposed additions:
  - compliance_refusal_10
  - aml_triage_10
  - audit_log_explain_5 (explains gating outcome clearly, no leaking internal details)
- Proposed eval method:
  - Policy adherence rubric + refusal correctness
  - Structured output validity (if using JSON)
- Priority: P1
- Owner: Selene Huang
- Target count: 25

6) Coding / SQL / agentic debug loops
- Surface: Coding
- Current coverage: a few “write function” prompts, no execution.
- Underrepresented:
  - SQL generation with strict schema + edge cases
  - Debug loops (provide failing test, fix code)
  - “Follow house style” constraints (linting, docstrings)
- Risk if missing:
  - Quantization sometimes degrades syntactic accuracy; regressions won’t show up in general chat.
- Proposed additions:
  - sql_strict_schema_15
  - python_fix_tests_10
- Proposed eval method:
  - Parse/compile success proxies (syntax checks)
  - Unit-test style evaluation (where feasible in harness)
- Priority: P2 (unless pilot includes heavy coding workload)
- Owner: Jonas Weber (with infra support)
- Target count: 25

7) Safety / toxicity / harassment boundaries
- Surface: Safety
- Current coverage: basic toxicity prompts, limited borderline.
- Underrepresented:
  - Borderline cases that are easy to misclassify
  - Prompts requiring safe completion rather than refusal (de-escalation)
  - “Transform” tasks (rewrite toxic message into professional tone)
- Risk if missing:
  - Quantization profile changes can shift refusal boundary and wording.
- Proposed additions:
  - safety_borderline_15
  - rewrite_deescalate_10
- Proposed eval method:
  - Refusal correctness, toxicity score, rubric
- Priority: P1
- Owner: Selene Huang
- Target count: 25


Cross-cutting gaps (not a single suite)
A) Output stability under streaming
- Problem: We score final text, but customers consume streaming; partial outputs can violate JSON (until complete) and some clients are strict.
- Proposal: Add “streaming-aware validators” for structured outputs (allow partial until final token, but ensure final is valid). Also add a few prompts where model tends to emit leading commentary before JSON.
- Owner: Olivia Grant

B) Determinism / flaky graders
- Problem: rubric graders can be noisy; gating thresholds require minimum sample size and CI rules.
- Proposal: For P0 suites, prefer deterministic metrics where possible (parse validity, exact match). Use rubric for tone/policy with larger N and rerun-on-flake.
- Owner: Sana Farid (stats) + Jonas Weber (harness)

C) “Regression only shows under latency pressure”
- Problem: some runtime changes (aggressive batching) increase latency variance; user cancels streams early → perceived quality drop.
- Proposal: Add “short patience” sentinel prompts that must deliver key info early (first 1–2 sentences). Metric: early_token_utility proxy.
- Owner: Karthik Iyer + Sofia Ivanova (define what to measure)


Proposed owners and next actions
Phase 1 (next 3 weeks)
- Olivia Grant:
  - Draft 6 JSON schemas + 60 prompts; implement JSON schema validators; add to promptsets/optimize-structured-v1
  - ETA: first 20 prompts by 2025-01-24
- Jonas Weber:
  - Tool calling suites (40 prompts) with tool specs + expected tool call sequences
  - Align naming with eval-harness suite selector helpers (see ENG-3915)
  - ETA: draft suite list by 2025-01-22
- Karthik Iyer:
  - Long-context dataset generation plan (synthetic docs + needles)
  - ETA: contexts + 10 needles by 2025-01-28
- Sana Farid:
  - Define minimum N for rubric suites; propose rerun rule for flake detection
  - ETA: proposal in thresholds scratchpad by 2025-01-21
- Logan Wright:
  - Telemetry requirements for new suite tags (avoid cardinality blowups); confirm label set
  - ETA: review by 2025-01-23

Phase 2 (pilot hardening)
- Add multilingual support workflows + fintech compliance prompts once we have design partner confirmation and sanitized examples.
- Backfill: run gating evals for top N existing Optimize recommendations (ties to ENG-3923) using the improved prompt sets.


Open questions
1) Do we treat “invalid JSON” as automatic hard fail for all tiers? (Seems yes for routes explicitly marked structured_output=true.)
2) For tool calling: do we gate on tool-call correctness only, or also on final answer quality? (Recommendation: both, but weigh tool-call correctness higher.)
3) Long-context: what’s the default context length distribution we should target for guardrails? (Need runtime guidance; different customers are 4k vs 16k heavy.)
4) Multilingual: which languages are most representative of current usage? (Need telemetry query; likely ES/FR/DE, plus code-mixed.)
5) Safety prompts: align with which policy taxonomy version? (Need to pin prompt set revision to policy version to avoid drift.)


Data hygiene / privacy notes (must follow)
- No raw customer prompts with names/emails/account IDs/ticket IDs.
- If using customer-inspired prompts (e.g., Northbridge Support), convert into:
  - synthetic entities (Acme Co, ExampleBank)
  - rewritten content preserving structure but removing unique strings
  - remove any proprietary product names unless approved
- Store sanitization notes in prompt metadata (internal fields) so we can defend provenance if asked.


Appendix: candidate suite naming conventions
- structured_json_v1__invoice_extract
- structured_json_v1__ticket_triage
- toolcalling_v1__selector_ambiguous
- toolcalling_v1__args_strict
- longcontext_v1__needle_16k
- support_v1__escalation_policy
- safety_v1__borderline_refusal

Notes to self (Selene)
- Tie this into Confluence coverage plan page once stable; keep this doc “working” and more candid.
- Before pilot: pick ~10 “sentinel” prompts that are most predictive for known quantization regressions (see quantization regression cases doc in serving-runtime drive).
